blocks.text: The Cloud App Control policy provides granular control over popular websites and applications. Cloud apps are organized by function into categories for easy reference and to facilitate defining rules for similar apps.
You can create rules to control how your users access specific cloud applications. For example, you can define a rule for instant messaging apps that allows chatting, but blocks file transfers.

The Cloud App Control policy rules can also be applied to Internet of Things (IoT) devices from a location or a sublocation that has the Enforce IoT Policy Control option enabled. You can apply the rules to IoT devices that are identified and classified (e.g., printers, sensors, etc.) by the Zscaler AI/ML under the IoT group in the Device Groups criterion.
The Cloud App Control policy provides the following benefits and enables you to:

blocks.item: Provide enhanced security and management of cloud application usage.
Monitor actions within cloud applications.
Allow administrators to set rules for applications and specific application instances.
Ensure secure data-usage policies.

blocks.text: Zscaler provides the Allow Unauthenticated Traffic for IoT Classifications predefined rules for all the categories. You can enable these rules to temporarily allow unauthenticated traffic that could be blocked by other rules, so that the Zscaler AI/ML can classify devices. These rules are disabled by default and cannot be deleted. You can modify the Rule Order, Rule Status, Rule Label, and Description for these rules and cannot edit other attributes.

Additionally, you can define a daily quota by bandwidth or time. When users browse these sites after their quota has been reached, the Zscaler service displays a message that explains that the content cannot be viewed because they exceeded their daily quota.
For information on the order in which the service enforces all policies, including this policy, see Understanding Policy Enforcement.

blocks.heading: About the Cloud App Control Policy Page

blocks.text: On the Cloud App Control Policy page (Data Security > Inline CASB > SaaS/Cloud App Policy), you can do the following:

blocks.item: View the configured Cloud App Control rules using one of the following options:
Application Category
Displays the rules based on the selected application category. By default, this option is selected.
Rules
Displays all the Cloud App Control rules with the predefined rules listed first, followed by configured rules.
Search for an application category.
Search for a Cloud App Control rule.
Add a Cloud App Control rule.
Select the column options to view the Cloud App Control rules accordingly.
The Rule Order and Actions columns are selected by default and they can't be unselected.
Enable or disable the filter for Cloud App Control rules.
Filter the Cloud App Control rule by Rule Label.
View a list of all configured Cloud App Control rules. For each rule, you can see the following:
Policy Rule Details
Rule Order: The policy rule order number. Cloud App Control rules are evaluated in ascending numerical order.
Admin Rank: The Admin Rank for this rule. This is only visible if you have enabled it in the Advanced Settings.
Rule Name: The name of the policy rule.
Rule Action: Displays whether the policy rule is disabled or what's set to Allow, Block, or Isolate.
The Isolate action is available only if Zero Trust Browser (formerly Isolation) is enabled for your organization and if the rule is not for DNS over HTTPS apps.
Rule Label: The label of the policy rule, if available.
Description: The description of the policy rule, if available.
Application Category: The application category of the policy rule, if available.
Cloud Applications: The cloud applications of the policy rule, if available.
Cloud Application Risk Profile: The cloud application risk profile of the policy rule, if available.
Cloud Application Instances: The cloud application instances of the policy rule, if available.
Users: The users of the policy rule, if available.
Groups: The groups of the policy rule, if available.
Departments: The departments of the policy rule, if available.
Locations: The locations of the policy rule, if available.
Location Groups: The location groups of the policy rule, if available.
Time: The time of the policy rule, if available.
Devices: The devices of the policy rule, if available.
Device Groups: The device groups of the policy rule, if available.
Device Trust Level: The device trust level of the policy rule, if available.
User Agents: The user agents of the policy rule, if available.
User Risk Profile: The user risk profile of the policy rule, if available.
Start Date and Time: The start date and time of the policy rule, if available. The rule is valid starting this date and time.
End Date and Time: The end date and time of the policy rule, if available. The rule ceases to be valid on this date and time.
Time Zone: The time zone in which the policy rule is valid.
Edit, duplicate, or delete a Cloud App Control rule.
